summary: A 36-check suite could not falsify its subject's DOTNET_ROOT export because every probe reached the SDK through the muxer, which ignores DOTNET_ROOT; the only consumer class that reads it (framework-dependent apphosts) was never exercised.
evidence: command:sed -i '/export DOTNET_ROOT="$candidate"/d' scripts/agent-env.sh && ./scripts/test-agent-env.sh (36 checks, 0 unexpected); file:scripts/test-agent-env.sh; issue:EHotwagner/S.I.R.#277
cost: none for this cycle; the unfalsifiable claim survived a full PR #260 review round and cost a separate board row to carry

summary: Building a real apphost inside the wired session under test turns an untestable environment variable into a falsifiable assertion, because the apphost reports the install its runtime was loaded from.
evidence: file:scripts/test-agent-env.sh; command:./scripts/test-agent-env.sh (38 checks, 0 unexpected; with the export deleted, exactly 1 WRONG at rc=1, the section I assertion)

summary: The dispatch brief's most promising suggested thread was a dead end for a structural reason the brief could not have known: scripts/fsgg-coord resolves through tier 4 (dotnet tool run) in this repository, which goes through the muxer and therefore can never discriminate DOTNET_ROOT; only tier 2's built apphost can, and it is not built here.
cost: one measurement round redirected; no rework

summary: The repair for an unevidenced claim itself shipped an unevidenced example: the replacement comment cited a tier-2 built fsgg-coord-engine apphost as a hot path, but src/FS.GG.Coord.Cli exists nowhere in this repository, which is a coord receiver resolving at tier 4 through the muxer. Caught by the independent actionability critic, not by the author or by the new check.
evidence: command:git ls-tree --name-only HEAD src/ (lists only SIR.* projects); file:scripts/fsgg-coord (a receiver resolves at tier 1/3/4 and never loads the file); file:scripts/agent-env.sh
cost: one artifact correction and a full re-run of the green/inversion/restore loop; caught before the PR was opened

summary: feedback-tool check-invalidation reports 17 errors identically on a clean origin/main..origin/main, so a worker cannot use it as a pass/fail signal for their own branch; the repo's wrapper gate scripts/test-feedback-audit-binding-exceptions.sh passes on the same head.
evidence: command:dotnet fsi .agents/skills/fs-gg-feedback-report/scripts/feedback-tool.fsx -- check-invalidation --base origin/main --head origin/main (17 errors); command:./scripts/test-feedback-audit-binding-exceptions.sh (rc=0); issue:EHotwagner/S.I.R.#252
cost: one dedupe investigation; no rework and nothing filed, the cause is already carried by S.I.R.#252

summary: The caller-inventory sentence in the repair was wrong twice in a row: first naming a tier-2 apphost this receiver repo cannot resolve, then naming the global tool shims as a hot path when no committed script in the repository invokes one as a bare command. Every tool call here goes through the muxer (dotnet fable, dotnet fsgg-sdd, dotnet tool run), which is itself the reason the old suite could not observe the export.
evidence: command:git grep -InE '(^|[^-a-zA-Z0-9_./])(fable|fsdocs|fantomas|paket|fake|fsgg-sdd)([^-a-zA-Z0-9_.]|$)' -- '*.sh' 'build.sh' '*.mjs' | grep -v 'dotnet ' (no bare command invocations); file:scripts/agent-env.sh; file:scripts/test-agent-env.sh
cost: two artifact corrections and three full green/inversion/restore loops; the second was caught by self-audit after the critic caught the first

summary: The suite mutates the real tracked scripts/agent-env.sh in section H, so a concurrent run emits a red that is indistinguishable from a genuine inversion (both are one WRONG at rc=1 in the same check); and its only trap was rm -rf on the directory holding the backup, so an interrupted run deleted the working tree's shim and its backup together.
evidence: command:kill -TERM a run stopped inside section H with the old trap (working tree loses scripts/agent-env.sh); command:./scripts/test-agent-env.sh with a live lock holder (REFUSED, exit 99); file:scripts/test-agent-env.sh
cost: one artifact fix plus its inversion evidence; the false red cost an independent reviewer one wasted measurement and a re-run

summary: The first version of the concurrency guard could not fail: after a losing mkdir it tested whether the lock directory existed, which reports the holder's lock as its own, so it ran normally against a live holder and returned 0. Inverting the guard before shipping is what exposed it.
evidence: command:mkdir the lockdir with a live pid then run ./scripts/test-agent-env.sh (first version: full green rc=0; fixed version: REFUSED exit 99); file:scripts/test-agent-env.sh
cost: none - caught at authoring time by the pnext-item rule that every added gate ships with evidence it can fail

summary: The check-invalidation red deduped three hops away from where it surfaced: S.I.R.#252 (closed, a different half of the symptom), then S.I.R.#258 (closed NOT_PLANNED, carrying the exact root cause), then FS-GG/.github#2856 (open, upstream, the live home). A worker deduping against the symptom or against the first-named row files a duplicate; only following the closure chain reaches the row that can hold the evidence.
evidence: issue:EHotwagner/S.I.R.#258; issue:FS-GG/.github#2856; command:gh issue view 258 --repo EHotwagner/S.I.R. (state CLOSED, reason NOT_PLANNED, re-routed)
cost: one root-cause investigation that would have produced a duplicate row had it stopped at the first or second hop

summary: The suite's documented [repo-root] argument silently tested the caller's shim instead of the one at that root: BASH_ENV carries a command substitution that bash evaluates at shell startup, before the -c body's cd ran, so git rev-parse resolved against the caller's cwd. With the target root's shim moved aside, the wired probes still resolved the pinned SDK and section H passed.
evidence: command:run the suite from one worktree against a second worktree's root with that root's shim moved aside - old fresh() reports the pinned version and section H passes, fixed fresh() reds correctly; file:scripts/test-agent-env.sh
cost: one wrong measurement while building a non-destructive reproduction; found because the base reproduction disagreed with the figure it was meant to confirm

summary: check-invalidation prints its invalidation listing only on the non-FAIL path, so while ledger errors are present - which is always, for any realistic diff - it never reports the merged-audit citations a commit actually invalidates. My first reading of the documented command concluded none of the errors were mine; two sealed citations in a merged audit were in fact invalidated by my change.
evidence: command:dotnet fsi .agents/skills/fs-gg-feedback-report/scripts/feedback-tool.fsx -- check-invalidation --changed 'scripts/test-agent-env.sh' (17 errors, no invalidation reported) versus the same run with the 13 ledgered paths added (reports 4 invalidated bindings incl. two for scripts/test-agent-env.sh); issue:FS-GG/.github#2856
cost: a real merge obligation was nearly missed: the exception-ledger entry owed for the 256 audit's stale citations

summary: The audit-binding exception ledger cannot be extended without also extending the wrapper gate's curated fixture, and extending that fixture demands an exception for every citation of the added audit that intersects the fixture's synthetic changed-set - including one whose digest never changed. Discharging a genuine obligation therefore requires fabricating a replacement record for a file nobody touched.
evidence: command:./scripts/test-feedback-audit-binding-exceptions.sh with the 256 audit added to the fixture (rc=1, three citations flagged: two genuine digest changes and one, scripts/ci-route.mjs, whose recorded digest aec19c9a equals the current file); file:scripts/test-feedback-audit-binding-exceptions.sh; issue:FS-GG/.github#2856
cost: a real obligation identified and deliberately left undischarged rather than satisfied with a fabricated ledger record
owner: FS-GG/.github#2856 - exception ledger and its wrapper fixture

summary: A commit SHA hand-transcribed into the cycle report was wrong, in a document whose entire purpose is verifiable evidence. It was caught only by running every hash in the document through git cat-file rather than by re-reading it.
evidence: command:for h in $(grep -oE '[0-9a-f]{40}' report.md | sort -u); do git cat-file -t $h; done (one UNRESOLVABLE before the fix, all resolve after)
cost: none - self-caught before the audit sealed; would have bound the audit to a nonexistent commit
